To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
strontium containing magnesium-zirconium alloys can be very useful in developing new biodegradable orthopaedic implants.
Mg-Zr biodegradable alloys containing appropriate quantities and ratios of calcium and strontium can be used to induce bone formation.

the addition of strontium to the Mg-Zr alloy system enhances the efficiency of bone formation in vivo, which is a very important finding that could have a significant impact on the development of new generation of biodegradable implants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel, biocompatible and biodegradable alloys that are useful in regenerative orthopedics.
the development of new biodegradables for regenerative orthopedics.
the development of biodegradable implants for orthopedic applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mg-Zr alloys, in general, are promising biodegradable orthopaedic materials, which could be further improved by the addition of suitable quantities of calcium or strontium.
Mg-Zr alloy with 2% strontium content was the most effective alloy in inducing osseointegration.
the Mg-Zr alloys are biocompatible and biodegradable, and can be considered for future development of biodegradable implants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the strontium content of the alloys plays a critical role in the biological properties of the implants.

the biodegradable Mg-Zr alloys could serve as an effective alternative to currently available metallic implants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Mg-Zr based biodegradable implant materials can be used to induce new bone formation in the vicinity of the implants, and that these implants can be used for regenerative orthopedics.
Mg-Zr based alloys with appropriate amounts of strontium are good candidates for developing biodegradable implants for orthopedic applications.
the biodegradable implant should be made of a material that can be degraded at a rate similar to bone healing and remodeling.
